messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors (telemetry / cloud / marketplace) - ACME Health

Hi Anna - thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can get you the artifacts your security and procurement teams asked for:

1) What we captured on the call:
- You need EU data residency (Ireland or Frankfurt).
- No user-identifiable PII should be sent to telemetry or third-party analytics vendors.
- Procurement wants a subprocessors list + short attestation for any telemetry/cloud provider that will process anything other than aggregated metrics.
- You asked about marketplace flows (where billing/partner integrations introduce a third-party) and whether any logs or metadata could leak customer data.

2) Action items we committed to:
- Share our current subprocessors spreadsheet and SOC 2 summary (attached).
- Note which telemetry vendors receive hashed identifiers vs. raw text and where redaction/pseudonymization is configurable.
- Describe default retention windows (PII/interaction content, telemetry, audit logs) and how to change them.
- Explain marketplace integration flow and whether partner metadata is ever combined with customer data.

I've attached our redwood-subprocessors-202706.xlsx and the SOC2-Report-Redwood-2026.pdf. Jonas and Neha are looped for technical specifics - pinged them for the vendor attestations you asked for.

Could you confirm: (a) the exact EU region you want enforced (IE/DE), and (b) whether your legal/regulatory team requires processor-level signed agreements from telemetry vendors (we can surface their contact/attestation info).

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up on Tuesday 6/22 to review the spreadsheet and any redlines. If procurement needs only the attestation doc + subprocessors list we can send that earlier.

Thanks -
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors (telemetry / cloud / marketplace) - ACME Health

Hi Marissa - thanks for the summary and for sending the attachments. Quick answers from our side:

- Region: We need Ireland (eu-west-1) for primary processing and storage. Replication to other regions is OK as long as primary residence is EU.
- Telemetry: We cannot have raw PII (names, email addresses, un-hashed user IDs) sent to telemetry/third-party analytics. Aggregated metrics are fine. For any vendor that receives user-level data we need a signed attestation confirming they will not use the data for other purposes and will maintain EU residency.
- Marketplace flow: We use a reseller marketplace for procurement; we need clarity on what metadata passes to the marketplace partner. Billing metadata is fine, but we must ensure application logs or prompt/response traces are never routed to that partner.

Can your team confirm which telemetry vendors you use by default and which of them are configurable (opt-in/out)? Also can you indicate default retention windows for: 1) prompt/response content, 2) audit logs (auth/changes), 3) telemetry/metrics?

If you can get the vendor attestation PDFs and the updated subprocessors sheet to procurement@acmehealth.com today that would be ideal; otherwise Wednesday latest.

Best,
Anna Lopez
Security & Privacy Lead | ACME Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T13:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors (telemetry / cloud / marketplace) - ACME Health

Hi Anna - looping in some technical detail from the runtime/telemetry side. Short answers here, happy to jump on a call to walk through specifics.

Telemetry vendors (default + notes):
- Datadog (default): receives aggregated metrics and traces. No raw prompt/response content by default. Option: can be configured to receive hashed user IDs only (SHA-256) for correlation; hashing salt is customer-scoped.
- Sentry (optional): error-level tracebacks; we can disable sending stack traces that include request/response bodies.
- Segment/analytics (optional): only aggregated events; we do not send PII unless the customer enables an integration.

Marketplace flow:
- Marketplace partner receives only billing and subscription metadata (customer name, plan id, invoice id).
- Application logs, prompt/response content, and debug traces never flow to marketplace partners unless explicitly enabled by the customer via a managed integration. We treat marketplace partners as processors with a narrow purpose and can add contractual restrictions per customer.

Retention defaults (configurable per-account):
- Prompt/response content: default 30 days. Options: 30 days / 90 days / custom (customer can request deletion via API or admin console).
- Audit logs (auth, config changes): default 365 days, can be extended to 7 years on Enterprise.
- Telemetry/metrics: 90 days aggregate by default. Raw traces (if enabled) 30 days.

Subprocessor attestations: we have vendor AUPs and SOC-type summaries for Datadog and our cloud provider. I will attach short attestation statements for Datadog and our primary cloud provider (AWS EU) for your procurement review. For telemetry vendors that would receive hashed IDs only, we can provide the hashing approach and sample config showing the opt-in toggle.

If you want, Jonas can show a quick demo of the admin toggles (redaction, hashing, retention) on our console.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
